errors: No mathematical errors found. All four constants (πi/24, πi/6, πi/6, −πi/6) are consistent with the leading-term normalizations, which I checked.
The theta series sign convention ((s+½)(z−½)) is consistent with the stated product. It equals the standard θ1(πz|ω) = −iΣ(−1)^n q^{(n+½)^2} e^{(2n+1)πiz}.
Minor: the region description ('im Innern des ... begrenzten ... Gebietes') is imprecise in the draft. Mathematically it must be the upper half-plane y>0.

results.what: Definition of η(ω) = q^{1/12}∏(1−q^{2ν}) with log η normalized by log η − πiω/12 → 0 as y→∞
results.modern_name: Dedekind eta function and its canonical logarithm
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind (Erläuterungen in Riemann's Werke, 1876/1877); the product itself goes back to Jacobi

results.what: η(2ω)η(ω/2)η((1+ω)/2) = e^{πi/24}η(ω)^3 and expressions of k^{1/4}, k'^{1/4}, √(2K/π) as eta quotients
results.modern_name: Eta-quotient expressions of Jacobi/Weber modular functions (Weber's f, f1, f2 relations)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi, Fundamenta nova (1829) §36; later systematized by Weber

results.what: Logarithmic versions (I) with exact branch constants
results.modern_name: Branch-normalized logarithms of modular lambda and theta-null
results.usually_credited_to: Dedekind (1876 Erläuterungen), following Jacobi Fund. nova §40

results.what: Programme of deducing behaviour at rational cusps from the unimodular theta transformation
results.modern_name: Cusp behaviour of modular forms; leads to the eta multiplier system and Dedekind sums

deep.surprise_reason: The page is Dedekind's draft of his published commentary in Riemann's Werke (the origin of Dedekind eta normalization and Dedekind sums), not Riemann's own work. Its contents are the published, well-known Dedekind text plus classical Jacobi identities.

checkable.asserts: k = 4 e^{πi/6} (η(2ω)/η((1+ω)/2))^4, i.e. formula (I) for log k (≈0)
Leading term check: RHS of log k minus log 4 equals πiω/2, consistent with log k − log 4√q → 0

transcription_corrections: The page is in Dedekind's hand (continuation of 'Erläuterungen ... von R. Dedekind'), not Riemann's.

'im Innern des Rechtecks [?] T begrenzten' is doubtful. The sense requires the region bounded by the real (abscissa) axis, i.e. the upper half-plane. The word before the 'x' is likely a reference to the axis x, not 'Rechteck'.
'1^{1/48}' should be read as e^{2πi/48} = e^{πi/24}. The margin notes e^{πi/24} (×3, partly struck) and e^{πi/12} are Dedekind's conversions of 1^{1/48} and 1^{-1/24} (the last with sign).

In the definition of the normalizations, the line reads 'log k − log 4 − ωπi/2 = log k − log 4√q', followed by 'log k' und log 2K/π ... mit q unendlich klein werden'. That is, all three tend to 0 as q→0.
